Heritage walk · Jammu and Kashmir

Heritage walk in Srinagar: old city, Mughal gardens and Pari Mahal

A heritage walk in Srinagar covers the old city (Shahr-e-Khas) along the Jhelum with the Jamia Masjid, Khanqah-e-Maula and Pathar Masjid, the Mughal gardens of Nishat, Shalimar and Chashme Shahi on Dal Lake, Pari Mahal, and older sites such as Harwan and the Shankaracharya temple. Pandrethan and Parihaspora are short drives away.

We arrange Srinagar heritage walks and study tours on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.

Why Srinagar matters

Srinagar has been the main city of the Kashmir valley for well over a thousand years. Kalhana's Rajatarangini, written in the 12th century in Sanskrit, is the best-known historical chronicle of early India and is set here, and the valley produced major Buddhist, Shaiva and Islamic traditions of learning.

Its architecture is distinctive. The wooden mosques and shrines of the old city, with tiered pyramidal roofs and spires, belong to a Himalayan building tradition unlike anything in the plains. The Mughal gardens on Dal Lake are among the finest surviving terraced gardens in the world, and Kashmiri crafts such as papier mâché, shawls and walnut carving have long histories in the city's mohallas.

Layers of Srinagar's history

Ashoka is traditionally linked with an early city in the valley. At Burzahom, near Srinagar, excavations found a Neolithic settlement with pit dwellings from about 3000 BCE, covered in the Stone Age in India guide. Harwan has a Buddhist site of about the 4th to 5th century CE with distinctive moulded terracotta tiles, and under the Karkota king Lalitaditya Muktapida in the 8th century large stone temples were built across the valley, including Parihaspora near Srinagar and Martand further south. Pandrethan has a small 10th century stone temple in the Kashmiri style.

Islam spread from the 14th century under the Shah Mir sultans and Sufi teachers such as Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani, remembered at Khanqah-e-Maula. Sultan Sikandar built the Jamia Masjid around 1400, and Zain-ul-Abidin (ruled 1420 to 1470) is remembered for patronage of crafts and tolerance. The Mughals took Kashmir in 1586 under Akbar, who built the Hari Parbat fort wall, and Jahangir, Nur Jahan and Shah Jahan's family laid out the gardens; Pari Mahal was built for Dara Shikoh. Afghan, Sikh and Dogra rule followed before 1947.

Using the Indo-Islamic architecture and Mughal architecture guides you can compare Srinagar's wooden mosques and gardens with the stone buildings of Delhi and Agra.

Places a heritage walk in Srinagar covers

  1. Jamia Masjid, Srinagar about 1400, rebuilt 17th century

    Congregational mosque with a courtyard of 378 deodar columns and brick walls.

  2. Khanqah-e-Maula 1395, rebuilt 1730s

    Wooden shrine on the Jhelum linked to Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani, with carved and painted interiors.

  3. Pathar Masjid 1623

    Stone mosque built by Nur Jahan, unusual in a city of timber mosques.

  4. Tomb of Zain-ul-Abidin's mother 15th century

    Brick tomb with glazed tiles and domes, built on an older temple plinth.

  5. Zaina Kadal and the Jhelum bridges 15th century onward

    Old bridges linking the mohallas of Shahr-e-Khas on both banks.

  6. Hari Parbat Akbar's wall 1590s, fort 18th century

    Hill with a Mughal wall and an Afghan-period fort, and shrines of several faiths on its slopes.

  7. Shankaracharya Temple rebuilt structure, early origins debated

    Stone temple on Takht-e-Sulaiman hill above Dal Lake; its date is debated by scholars.

  8. Nishat Bagh 1633

    Terraced garden laid out by Asaf Khan, Nur Jahan's brother, with twelve terraces.

  9. Shalimar Bagh 1619, extended 1630

    Jahangir's garden for Nur Jahan, with a central water channel and black marble pavilion.

  10. Chashme Shahi 1632

    Small Mughal garden built around a spring.

  11. Pari Mahal 1640s to 1650s

    Terraced garden and school built for Dara Shikoh above the lake.

  12. Harwan about 4th to 5th century CE

    Buddhist site with apsidal shrine and moulded terracotta tiles, near the Shalimar garden.

  13. Pandrethan Temple about 10th century

    Small Kashmiri stone temple standing in a tank, on the old route out of the city.

Walking routes in Srinagar

Shahr-e-Khas on foot

About 3 hours

Jamia Masjid, Srinagar → Tomb of Zain-ul-Abidin's mother → Zaina Kadal and the Jhelum bridges → Khanqah-e-Maula → Pathar Masjid

The Mughal gardens

Half a day, by vehicle

Chashme Shahi → Pari Mahal → Nishat Bagh → Shalimar Bagh → Harwan

Hills and early temples

Half a day, by vehicle

Hari Parbat → Shankaracharya Temple → Pandrethan Temple

Museums in Srinagar

  • Sri Pratap Singh (SPS) Museum. Kashmir's main museum, with Harwan tiles, sculpture, manuscripts, shawls and papier mâché.
  • Burzahom site. Neolithic and Megalithic site about 16 km from the city, interpreted on site.

Best time for a walk

April to October. Spring for the gardens, autumn for clear weather; winters are very cold.

What you see on a walk

In the old city, look at timber and brick (dhajji dewari and taq) construction, carved latticework (pinjrakari) and the tiered roofs of Khanqah-e-Maula. The Jamia Masjid's courtyard is lined with 378 deodar wood columns. On the Jhelum, the old bridges (kadal) connect the mohallas.

In the gardens, read the Mughal plan: a central water channel running down terraces from a spring, with pavilions and cascades. The lecture Sacred architecture across communities suits a group that wants to compare mosques, shrines and temples, and Reading Sarada script connects directly to Kashmir, where the Sarada script was used for Sanskrit and Kashmiri.

Srinagar for school and college groups

Srinagar visits are arranged as a study tour built for your group. Students can prepare with Introductory Prakrit or the Sarada course, and with the lecture on India's scripts from Brahmi to Sarada.

The old city walk from the Jamia Masjid to Khanqah-e-Maula and the Jhelum bridges is about 2 km. The gardens along Dal Lake are spread out and need a vehicle, as do Harwan, Burzahom, Pandrethan and Parihaspora. Dress modestly for mosques and shrines, and check the current travel advisory and site access before you go.

How we run this

  • Schools: a Srinagar study tour on the Mughal gardens and the old city.
  • Colleges: a Sarada script course before a field visit to Kashmir.
  • Families: a private garden and old city day with a historian.

Questions people ask

What are the main historical places in Srinagar?

The Jamia Masjid, Khanqah-e-Maula and Pathar Masjid in the old city; Hari Parbat; the Mughal gardens of Nishat, Shalimar and Chashme Shahi; Pari Mahal; the Shankaracharya temple; and older sites at Harwan and Pandrethan.

Who built the Mughal gardens in Srinagar?

Shalimar Bagh was laid out by Jahangir in 1619, Nishat Bagh by Asaf Khan in 1633, Chashme Shahi under Shah Jahan in 1632, and Pari Mahal for Dara Shikoh in the 1640s to 1650s.

Is a Srinagar heritage walk suitable for schools?

Yes. The gardens are open and easy to manage, and the old city walk suits older students in small groups. Check current advisories and plan vehicles between clusters.

Which museum in Srinagar is best for history?

The SPS Museum on the Jhelum is the main museum, with archaeology from Harwan and other sites, manuscripts, textiles and crafts.

Can Talaash Heritage arrange a Kashmir study tour?

Yes, on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.
